where: Section 2 (Proof by squaring), the sentence after the proof of the upper-tail form
problem: The sentence is cut off and unreadable: "The complement of |X − μ| ≥ kσ is |X − μ|  0." The event and the conclusion of the inside form are lost, so a student cannot follow the complement step that produces P(|X − μ| < kσ) ≥ 1 − 1/k².
fix: The complement of the event |X − μ| ≥ kσ is |X − μ| < kσ. So P(|X − μ| < kσ) = 1 − P(|X − μ| ≥ kσ) ≥ 1 − 1/k². This step needs kσ > 0, that is k > 0 and σ > 0.

where: Section 1, last paragraph of the section (moment inequalities remark)
problem: It says Chebyshev uses E[X] and E[(X − μ)²], "the first two moments". E[(X − μ)²] is the second central moment, not the second moment E[X²]; Markov alone uses the first moment and Chebyshev alone uses only the second central moment.
fix: Some syllabi call Markov and Chebyshev moment inequalities because between them they use the first moment E[X] and the second central moment E[(X − μ)²] = σ².

problem: "Chebyshev gives a lower bound, not an upper bound" is too broad. The chapter itself teaches an upper bound, P(|X − μ| ≥ kσ) ≤ 1/k²; only the inside statement is a lower bound. A student may conclude Chebyshev has no upper-tail form.
fix: No. The statement P(|X − μ| < 2σ) ≥ 0.75 is a lower bound on the probability of being inside the interval, so the true value 0.92 is allowed. (The matching upper bound is on the outside event: P(|X − μ| ≥ 2σ) ≤ 0.25, and 0.08 ≤ 0.25.)
